newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower and awaits next move.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower and awaits next move.

text.p: Gold price steadiness focused attention on Tuesday morning after fund managers disillusioned with the market's lack of progress unwound their holdings late on Monday.
"Now the key support is at $346/$345 and that needs to survive or the $340.00 will be in danger," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Gold was fixed at $347.40 per ounce, down $4.00 from Monday afternoon and a close of $350.00/$350.50.

Gold's repeated failures to break through $355.00 was cited as one reason why the funds began to sell late on Monday on Comex, igniting sell stops and taking the exchange's April futures contract down $4.70 to $348.30 by the close.

The Swiss parliament beginning its debate on loosening strictures on the Swiss National Bank's management of investments and gold reserves was a sentiment issue more than a physical one, dealers said.
"The $347.00 should hold at least during European trading. What happens in New York is another matter," one dealer said.
He added that steadiness in silver above $5.20 seemed to be helping bullion hold its ground especially during early pressure to test the downside.
Suddenly the very low Comex open interest as evidence that the funds had covered their short gold positions was a matter of concern, they said.
"The funds are not as short as they were. The worry is now that they have seen the upside limited and will renew larger short positions," one dealer said.
Silver was pushed towards a breakdown through $5.20 in New York last night and again on Tuesday morning when gold was weaker, but both times the level held.
"Silver could go quickly if it does go," one dealer warned.
A test of $5.09 was technically possible, analysts said.
Also on a technical basis, the gold-silver ratio looked like it was trying to test 65/64 after coming below 67 on Monday.
Platinum and palladium were both marked down with gold.
Dealers said there was no firmer news on when Russia's negotiators would open 1997 contract talks with Japan or when the first shipments of the year would start to move.
"A sharp movement will be a forerunner of an announcement that talks or shipments have started " a dealer said.
Platinum was indicated $1.50 lower at $377.75/$378.75 and palladium was $$3.25 off the close at $148.50/$149.50. --Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
